unit.why: A single narrative, quoted from the book רמ״ז: the rabbi of Gritza comes to the Seer of Lublin to mock him, and is won over when the Seer perceives at a distance how his friend R. Zusha treated a guest.

stories.start_quote: ובס׳ רמ״ז כתב וז״ל הה״ג הק׳
stories.summary_en: The rabbi of Gritza goes to the Seer of Lublin's third Sabbath meal to mock him but is drawn to him. He submits a kvitel for himself and his friend R. Zusha, and the Seer first condemns and later praises Zusha. They then learn that Zusha had shamed a learned guest at that time and afterwards made amends and helped him with money, so they recognize the Seer's holy spirit and return to him.

tags.why: Came to mock and was drawn close; both travel back to the Seer.

quotes: אז ראו כי רוה״ק שורה בתוך בית מדרשו
אז דבר הרבי על הרב מו״ה זושיא הנ״ל דברים לא טובים
tags.why: The Seer knows Zusha's conduct from afar.

quotes: בעת נסיעתו משם נתן פעם ב׳ קוויטיל
tags.why: Kvitlakh are submitted to the rebbe.

quotes: אצל הרה״ק אור ישראל הרבי מלובלין ז״ל לשחוק ממנו
tags.why: A skeptical scholar comes to mock the rebbe.
The encounter takes place at the third Sabbath meal.

quotes: מה זה עשיתי לא די שלא ראיתי מעות
tags.why: Zusha regrets his deed and makes amends.

quotes: אז נחלש דעת האורח והלך ממנו בפחי נפש

tags.why: Zusha gives money to the poor guest.
The Seer's puzzling words are understood afterwards.

quotes: נכנס אצל רעו הנ״ל וספר לו הכל

tags.why: The story is framed as quoted from an earlier book.
